# preview/ — what each capture shows

Two families, two provenance rules. A capture is only useful if its name says
what it shows and this file says how to reproduce it (airhorn-7q0x).

## Generated by tool — do not hand-edit

`node tools/preview-evidence.mjs --out preview` writes these (it fails if any is
missing, and `evidence.json` records the same run):

| file | state captured |
| --- | --- |
| `horn-light.png` | default desktop viewport, light scheme, idle |
| `horn-dark.png` | same, `prefers-color-scheme: dark` |
| `horn-320.png` | 320px viewport at DPR 2 |
| `horn-offline.png` | after first load + service worker activation, offline reload — the **only** capture in which the status caption paints, since `#app-status` is a 1px box until the app has something to say |
| `evidence.json` | the same run's published files, sizes and gzip sizes |

The install control's painted state in these depends on whether Chrome offered
an install at capture time, so a regeneration can differ there for reasons
unrelated to the change under review.

## Captured from the test suites — copied in by hand

`node tests/visual-overrides.test.mjs` writes its screenshots to
`/tmp/airhorn-visual-overrides/<sha>-<stamp>/`; the files below are copies of
those, so the suite is their source of truth.

| file | shows | typed tier in frame |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `typography-before.png` | boot-failure card before the system font stack (serif Times body copy) | body 16px + button 15px |
| `typography-after.png` | the same card after the stack change | body 16px/400 + button 15px/500 |
| `typography-fallback-heading.png` | stylesheets blocked, `.stylesheet-failed` → `.horn-label` renders (`7-typography-fallback-heading.png`) | heading 20px/600 |

`typography-before.png` and `typography-after.png` are a historical pair from
the capture that motivated the change; the "before" state no longer exists in
the tree, so only "after" can be regenerated.

## The display tier has no capture, on purpose

The scale's display tier (32px/700) is applied to the `h1`, which is visually
hidden by design (the horn disc carries the page and the accessible name comes
from `aria-label`). Nothing paints it, so nothing can photograph it — it is a
scale for future UI, not a rendered tier today. Likewise the live horn screen
carries no body-size copy at all: its only painted text is the 15px install
control and the 14px status caption, which is why the caption tier's evidence is
`horn-offline.png` rather than a second screenshot of the idle page.

Two captures were deleted in airhorn-7q0x: `typography-hierarchy.png` (stale,
superseded, referenced nowhere) and `typography-active-hierarchy.png` (a
byte-identical duplicate of it that showed the boot-failure card, not the
caption tier its name claimed).
